sector_model: Online gaming operator, Up-C with tax receivable agreement: P/E on total economic income, FCF after capitalized software and licenses, TRA liability, regulatory and tax exposure; per-share values use Class A plus Class V units.
thesis: Rush Street Interactive (NYSE: RSI), online casino and sports betting in 16 U.S. states, Canada and Latin America, Up-C structure. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-29) read in relevant sections. Q3 revenue 385.9M (+38.8%), 9M revenue 1,150.0M vs 809.5M (+42.1%); 9M pretax 142.2M, tax 58.1M (40.8% effective), total NI 84.2M of which 51.7M belongs to non-controlling interests; 9M Adjusted EBITDA 187.0M vs 109.5M (non-GAAP). Cash 381.9M, no debt; 9M OCF 143.3M vs 95.9M. Close 11.225 (2026-11-20) x 230.60M Class A plus Class V units = 2.59B = 25.1x TTM total NI 103.3M, FCF yield 7.0% (before about 10M of 9M license and intangible payments), 7.1x book (own arithmetic). Fell 5.6% over the prior five sessions. Possible market view: a regulated, tax-exposed, competitive U.S. betting operator at peak growth. Differing evidence: sustained 39 to 42% growth, rising cash conversion, no debt. Not a recommendation.
counterthesis: Gaming tax increases and new state restrictions, customer acquisition costs and competition from large operators and prediction markets can erase margins; the 40.8% effective tax rate and the 243.4M tax receivable agreement liability (85% of tax benefits payable to unit holders; only 1.1M paid in 9M) reduce shareholder cash. Class V holders own 50.1% of units, so a Class A per-share view overstates ownership; share count differs by class basis. Revenue growth is partly Latin America and new markets and may slow. 2025 results contained a 102.8M tax benefit and 106.6M other expense that distort comparisons. Peers (DraftKings, Flutter, Sportradar) and history not compared; state-level exposure not analysed.
invalidation: Invalidated by growth falling below about 15% with rising marketing cost, adverse state gaming tax changes, cash conversion falling well below NI, TRA payments consuming operating cash, or loss of key state licenses.
